note: Vehicle catalog served at /v1/vehicles (ADR-020). The app caches this and sends the resolved vehicle with each plan, so a rider's edits behave exactly like a catalog entry. Every entry carries where its numbers came from and how much to trust them: 'verified' = read off the manufacturer's own spec page or sheet, 'derived' = computed from published figures (shown in the formula), 'press' = reputable coverage only, 'unverified' = plausible but unconfirmed, do not rely on it. Ranges are manufacturer claims and optimistic by nature; the energy model stays pessimistic regardless. Zero labels its highway figures 'Low-Speed' and 'High-Speed Highway Commuting' and no longer publishes the speeds behind them; older sheets used 55 and 70 mph and that mapping is likely but unverified, so don't treat it as Zero's claim. Zero's US pages are MY2025 — there is no published MY2026 US spec. The Zero SR (naked) is discontinued, and the XE/XB are omitted: Zero quotes their range at 31 mph and they top out near 50 mph, which puts them outside what this app plans for.

vehicles.notes: 12.6 kW needs the $3,000 dealer-fit 6 kW Rapid Charging Module, which excludes the Power Tank. Power Tank ($3,200) takes the pack to nearly 21 kWh max; Zero doesn't publish the resulting nominal capacity or range. DC fast charging announced 2026-09-03 for 2027 models, retrofittable to MY2022+ — nothing ships today.
Rapid Charger adds 6 kW; Zero publishes charge times rather than a combined kW for this model, so 12.6 is arithmetic, not their claim.

Only a 3.3 kW onboard charger as standard — half the SR/S — so charge stops are long unless the rider has the $3,000 Rapid Charger. Combined 9.3 kW is arithmetic, not a Zero claim. US-only; absent from the EU MY2026 lineup.

vehicles.notes: Level 2 is useless on this bike: LiveWire states it 'is not compatible with Level 2 Charging' and an L2 station charges it no faster than a household socket, so plan DC (CCS1) stops only.
